## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. He frowned and turned away  (`#he-frowned-and-turned-away`)

Cited ayat: 80:1-10

> **80:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ
>
> **80:2** أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ
>
> **80:3** وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُۥ يَزَّكَّىٰٓ
>
> **80:4** أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ
>
> **80:5** أَمَّا مَنِ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
>
> **80:6** فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ
>
> **80:7** وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ
>
> **80:8** وَأَمَّا مَن جَآءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ
>
> **80:9** وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ
>
> **80:10** فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ

### Claims

**c1** (80:1-2): The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him.

**c2** (80:3): The verse asks the one addressed what would let him know: perhaps the blind man might purify himself.

**c3** (80:4): He might also be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him.

**c4** (80:5-6): As for the one who considers himself in no need, the one addressed attends to him.

**c5** (80:7): It is not upon the one addressed if that one does not purify himself.

**c6** (80:8-10): As for the one who came to the one addressed striving, and he fears, the one addressed is distracted from him.

### One-minute summary

The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him [c1]. It says that the blind man might purify himself or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him [c2][c3]. It speaks of the one who came striving, and fears, and from whom attention was turned [c6].

### Complete story

The passage tells that someone frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him [c1].

The verse then asks the one addressed what would let him know: perhaps the blind man might purify himself [c2], or he might be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him [c3].

As for the one who considers himself in no need, the one addressed attends to him [c4]. It is not upon the one addressed if that one does not purify himself [c5]. And as for the one who came to the one addressed striving, and he fears, the one addressed is distracted from him [c6].

### Deep study

The passage begins by speaking of someone who frowned and turned away, and goes on to speak directly to the one addressed [c1][c2]. It sets one person beside another: one who considers himself in no need and is attended to, and one who came striving and fearing and is not [c4][c6]. It names the possible benefit to the blind man as purifying himself and being reminded [c2][c3], and says what is not upon the one addressed [c5].

### Kids mode

The passage tells of a blind man who came, and of someone who frowned and turned away [c1]. It says that the blind man might have been reminded, and that the reminder would have helped him [c3]. It speaks of the one who came striving and fearing [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage turns attention toward the one who comes striving and fearing [c6]. Another is that it sets the one who considers himself in need of nothing beside the one who comes seeking [c4][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the blind man is. The verses say only 'the blind man' and give no name.
- Not established: who frowned and turned away. The first verses use a verb with 'he', and the verses that follow speak to 'you'; that they are the same person is an inference from the change of address, and the draft does not state it.
- Not established: who the one is who considers himself in no need, where this took place, or when.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the blind man, the identity of the one who frowned and the occasion. None is used in the story texts, and this draft names no one.
